extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: TextVQA is a dataset designed to benchmark VQA models on their ability to read and reason about text in images. It contains 45,336 questions on 28,408 images from the Open Images dataset, focusing on images from categories that tend to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard). Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers provided by humans. Questions require reading and reasoning about text in the image to answer correctly.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research, Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.citeAs: Singh, A., Natarajan, V., Shah, M., Jiang, Y., Chen, X., Batra, D., Parikh, D., & Rohrbach, M. (2019). Towards VQA Models That Can Read. arXiv:1904.08920
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through a three-stage crowd-sourcing pipeline. In the first stage, annotators identified images containing text. In the second stage, 1-2 questions were collected for each image, requiring reading text to answer. In the third stage, 10 answers were collected for each question. Hand-crafted questions with known answers were used to identify and filter out bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were sourced from the Open Images v3 dataset. Training and validation images were collected from Open Images' training set, while test set was collected from Open Images' test set. Categories likely to contain text (e.g., billboard, traffic sign, whiteboard) were selected by running the Rosetta OCR system on sample images and using normalized per-category OCR box counts as sampling weights.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images without text (identified in first stage) were filtered out, resulting in 28,408 images. Questions marked as problematic by a majority of workers (no text in image, not a question, answering doesn't require reading text, unanswerable) were removed. Bad annotators identified through hand-crafted test questions were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three-stage annotation: (1) Annotators identify if images contain text via yes/no flag. (2) For each image, annotators provide 1-2 questions requiring reading text to answer; for the second question, they see the first and must create a different question with a different answer. (3) 10 answers collected per question, with instructions similar to VQA and VizWiz datasets, plus four quality flags (no text, not a question, doesn't require reading, unanswerable).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All 10 annotators agree on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, while 3 or more annotators agree on the most common answer for 97.9% of questions. Human accuracy evaluated at 85.01% on validation and 86.79% on test.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system (used for OCR token extraction and for identifying image categories likely to contain text)
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses a critical need for visually impaired users, as the VizWiz study found up to 21% of questions from visually-impaired users involve reading and reasoning about text in images. TextVQA is intended to encourage research on improving text detection/recognition and enabling VQA models to aid visually impaired users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model trained on the dataset shows a bias toward predicting 'new york' for city-related questions. The most common answer 'yes' accounts for only 4.71% of majority answers. Questions often start with 'what' and frequently ask about time, names, brands, or authors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The OCR system used (Rosetta) fails at detecting text that is rotated, unstructured (e.g., scribbles), or partially occluded. 8.9% of TextVQA questions require combining multiple OCR tokens to answer, which is left as future work. The dataset is limited to text in natural everyday scenes (not bar charts, textbook diagrams, etc.).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation for VQA models that require reading and reasoning about text in images. The dataset is split into 34,602 training, 5,000 validation, and 5,734 test questions. Intended to benchmark progress complementary to VQA 2.0, especially for applications aiding visually impaired users.
